cards.title: Spoon Ferry Sees the Harbor
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led printable paper viewpoint card to let writers tell a lunchbox-harbor scene from a pretend spoon ferry's view in the kitchen-window paper frame: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: place the spoon ferry, lunchbox dock, crumb waves, and napkin flag paper pieces in the pretend frame; choose the object narrator: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: With the adult, work offline on this paper card. Pretend the spoon ferry is telling the scene and write what it notices first: ____________________.
cards.firstViewPrompt: First view: I am the spoon ferry, and the lunchbox harbor appears like ____________________.
cards.secondViewPrompt: Second view: A snack-barge helper sees the same harbor and notices ____________________.
cards.nearDetailPrompt: Near detail: Close to the ferry, I can see ____________________.
cards.farDetailPrompt: Far detail: Across the paper harbor, I can see ____________________.
cards.thoughtCluePrompt: Thought clue: The spoon ferry thinks, If I glide carefully, ____________________.
cards.reviseViewPrompt: Revise view: Change 'The ferry moved' so the spoon ferry tells it: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: circle one paper harbor item and finish one object-view sentence: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Carry-away line: try the object view again with a new pretend lunchbox cargo: ____________________.

cards.title: Acorn Cart From Two Desks
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led printable paper viewpoint card to compare the same acorn errand scene from two invented helper desks in the kitchen-window paper frame: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: set down the acorn cart, button counter, leaf stamp desk, and paper path slip; choose two helper roles: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: With the adult, work offline on this paper card. Tell the acorn mix-up twice, once from each helper's view: ____________________.
cards.firstViewPrompt: First view: The Button Counter Helper thinks the acorn cart matters because ____________________.
cards.secondViewPrompt: Second view: The Leaf Stamp Helper tells the same moment and notices ____________________.
cards.nearDetailPrompt: Near detail: On the desk nearest the acorn cart, one clue is ____________________.
cards.farDetailPrompt: Far detail: At the far paper shelf, another helper can see ____________________.
cards.thoughtCluePrompt: Thought clue: One helper keeps thinking, The best next stop is ____________________.
cards.reviseViewPrompt: Revise view: Change 'The cart was confusing' into a view from one helper: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: point to one helper role and write only that helper's view sentence: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Carry-away line: retell the same errand scene from a new pretend desk: ____________________.

cards.title: Map Room Through Seed Shelves
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led printable paper viewpoint card to help writers let the map-room setting shape what the narrator notices in a fictional kitchen-window frame: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: arrange seed packet drawers, a folded garden map, blank path cards, and a small table label; choose the setting lens: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: With the adult, work offline on this paper card. Choose Map Keeper, Seed Shelf Guide, or Path Card, then write what the room makes that narrator notice: ____________________.
cards.firstViewPrompt: First view: From the map table, the most important clue is ____________________.
cards.secondViewPrompt: Second view: From the seed shelf, the same clue appears as ____________________.
cards.nearDetailPrompt: Near detail: Beside the folded map, I notice ____________________.
cards.farDetailPrompt: Far detail: At the far side of the packet drawers, I notice ____________________.
cards.thoughtCluePrompt: Thought clue: The narrator wonders whether the missing path means ____________________.
cards.reviseViewPrompt: Revise view: Change 'The room had seeds' into a setting-lens sentence with one map-room clue: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: choose one seed packet shape and write a setting-lens phrase beside it: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Carry-away line: use the same map-room setting with a new narrator role: ____________________.

cards.title: Gauge Tube Close-Up Train
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led printable paper viewpoint card to start a railway scene with one close object detail before the whole fictional view: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: place the clear gauge tube, bead cards, shiny rail strip, and tiny train piece in the pretend kitchen-window frame; choose the close clue: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: With the adult, work offline on this paper card. Begin beside the gauge tube, then widen the view in one sentence: ____________________.
cards.firstViewPrompt: First view: The Gauge Checker sees the railway from beside the measuring tube and notices ____________________.
cards.secondViewPrompt: Second view: The Train Conductor sees the same scene from the cab and notices ____________________.
cards.nearDetailPrompt: Near detail: At the tube edge, one tiny clue is ____________________.
cards.farDetailPrompt: Far detail: Along the far rail strip, the larger pattern is ____________________.
cards.thoughtCluePrompt: Thought clue: The Gauge Checker suspects the clue means ____________________.
cards.reviseViewPrompt: Revise view: Change 'It was rainy' into a close-detail sentence about one object: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: point to the tube, bead card, or rail strip and write one close-detail phrase: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Carry-away line: make a second railway view that begins with one tiny gauge clue: ____________________.

cards.title: Moss Signal Mind Glow
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led printable paper viewpoint card to add a narrator thought clue to a fictional observatory scene in the kitchen-window paper frame: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: place moss tile cards, a dome chart, signal shapes, and two narrator labels; choose the hidden thought clue: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: With the adult, work offline on this paper card. Write what the observer sees, then add one thought that hints at what they believe: ____________________.
cards.firstViewPrompt: First view: The Dome Observer sees the moss signal as ____________________.
cards.secondViewPrompt: Second view: The Note Keeper sees the same signal as ____________________.
cards.nearDetailPrompt: Near detail: Beside the glowing moss tile, one small sign is ____________________.
cards.farDetailPrompt: Far detail: Across the pretend dome chart, another sign is ____________________.
cards.thoughtCluePrompt: Thought clue: The observer does not say the answer yet, but thinks ____________________.
cards.reviseViewPrompt: Revise view: Change 'The observer was worried' into a thought clue that shows the feeling: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: choose a glow, blink, or hush card and write one quiet thought on paper: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Carry-away line: retell the observatory moment with one new thought clue: ____________________.
